headline: Bond vigilantes, Gulf oil shock and floods force a grudging era of financial repression

events: French government falls over budget; OAT-Bund spread hits 190bp and ECB activates TPI for the first time, triggering a legal fight with Germany's constitutional court
UK gilt sell-off after unfunded defence and energy-support package; BoE pauses QT and Chancellor resigns
US extends Section 232 tariffs to semiconductors and pharma; China retaliates with tightened rare-earth and gallium licensing
Record South Asian heatwave and failed monsoon cut Indian wheat output; India bans rice exports again
AI capex boom peaks; first big write-down at a hyperscaler-linked data-center REIT
Israel-Iran war re-escalates; Houthi and Iranian attacks close Hormuz to tankers for five weeks, Brent spikes to $148
European gas hits EUR 120/MWh in winter; G20 inflation averages 6.8%, Fed and ECB hike 75bp into a slowdown
US presidential election fought on cost of living; narrow winner promises tariff 'dividend' cheques financed by deficit
Egypt, Pakistan and Kenya default or seek restructuring; Common Framework stalls as China and Gulf creditors demand seniority
Global equity correction of 30% as AI-infrastructure debt is repriced; private-credit funds gate redemptions
Weak 30-year US Treasury auction and term-premium blowout push 10-year yield to 6.4%; Fed launches 'market-functioning' purchases and caps bank SLR, a de facto yield-curve control
Japan's JGB 30-year breaches 4.5%; BoJ resumes unlimited buying and yen falls to 190 per dollar
World enters recession (global growth 0.6%); global unemployment peaks at 6.6%
China-Taiwan 'quarantine' standoff: PLA coast-guard inspections of Taiwan-bound shipping for 11 weeks; chip prices triple before a negotiated easing
Category-5 hurricane and Gulf Coast refinery damage plus Pakistan floods; Florida home-insurance market effectively nationalised
Financial repression era: Basel liquidity rules rewritten to force banks and pensions to hold more domestic sovereign debt; real rates held negative
Italy requires an ESM precautionary line after spreads spike; EU agrees a second joint-borrowing facility for defence and energy (EUR 600bn)
Sahel-coastal West Africa conflict spills into Ghana and Benin borders; Ethiopia-Eritrea war over Red Sea access
AI agents widely deployed in back-office and customer service; layoffs in BPO hubs (Philippines, India) spark protests
Emergency solar, batteries and nuclear life-extensions accelerate as oil-shock memory reshapes energy policy; coal also rebounds in Asia
Fragile recovery: global growth 2.7% but inflation stuck near 4% in the US and UK as central banks tolerate overshoot
Ukraine frozen-conflict armistice along contact line, with no settlement; Europe's defence spending reaches 3% of GDP
Argentina, Turkey-adjacent frontier markets and Sri Lanka (again) among nine sovereign distress cases since 2027
Wealth taxes and windfall levies introduced in several European states; populist parties lead governments or coalitions in 5 of G7
Global average temperature anomaly hits 1.6C in an El Nino year; insured disaster losses exceed $250bn

winners: Holders of real assets and commodity producers (Gulf states with alternative pipelines, Norway, Canada, Australia)
India and Mexico as diversified 'connector' manufacturing hubs despite food-price strain
Large AI platform firms that survived the 2028 capex washout with pricing power
losers: Savers and bondholders hit by negative real rates
Import-dependent low-income countries in Africa and South Asia
Young renters and first-time buyers in Anglosphere cities
Back-office and BPO workers in the Philippines and India
Climate-exposed homeowners in Florida, Gulf Coast and southern Europe
bullets: Advanced-economy bond markets are quietly managed: central banks cap long yields, and regulation herds domestic savings into government debt.
Inflation has settled around 3.5-4% rather than 2%, eroding debt ratios slowly while squeezing wages and pensions.
Trade runs through rival US- and China-centred blocs with a contested middle; tariffs, export controls and shipping-insurance premia are permanent costs.
The 2028 Hormuz shock turned energy security into the main driver of decarbonisation: solar, storage and nuclear grew fast, but so did Asian coal.
AI is mainstream in a third of firms, displacing tens of millions of routine service jobs and widening the gap between capital owners and workers.
Nine sovereign debt crises since 2027 have overwhelmed the creditor architecture; IMF resources are stretched and aid budgets keep shrinking.
Politics is angrier and more populist; trust in institutions is at a generational low and climate-disaster relief is a constant fiscal fight.
Europe is more fiscally integrated and better armed than in 2026, the one structural silver lining of the cascade.
wildcard: The 2029 PLA 'quarantine' of Taiwan-bound shipping, which tripled chip prices for a quarter before a face-saving inspection deal.
image_description: In a sweltering Marseille evening in 2031, a family sits on their balcony under a rationed-AC timer while a neighbour's phone app shows the day's capped bond-coupon savings rate, a rooftop solar array glints above, and a delivery drone hums past a banner protesting the latest pension freeze.
